Introduction 
2.3-Menoh are an important class of functiondized 
allenes, which can be used as the starting materials for 
the synthesis of oximes,’ 2,5-dihydrofimn~,~ a- 
methylenela~tone,~ a- or 7- amino alcohols,4 and a , /?- 
unsaturated ketones. ‘Ihese compounds were usually ~re- 
pared by reductive elimination of mono-0-tetrahydropy- 
ran-2-yl or alkoxy derivatives of butyne-l,4-diol~,~ tran- 
sition metal-mediated or -catalyzed reaction of I-akynyl 
epoxides,’ the reaction of Grignard reagents with 4-hy- 
droxy-2-alkynyl chlorides, hydrolysis of 2,3-allenyl bro- 
mides,’ treatment of allylic alcohols with : CBrz and 
RLi,*O electrochemical reaction of aldehydes or ketones 
with propargylic bromides, I’ Cd2-mediated reaction of 
aldehydes or ketones with propargylic brwnides,” and 
CuBr-mediated reaction of terminal propargylic alcohols 
with paraformaldehyde. l3 In this paper we wish to report a 
facile synthesis of substituted 2,3-denoh via the duc- 
tion of 2,3-aUenoates. 
Treatment of ethyl 2-methyl4phenyl-2, 3-buta- 
dienoate ( la) with 4.0 equiv. of DIBAL-H solution in 
cyclohexane at mom temperature afforded a complicated 
mixture (Entry 1, Table 1). ?he reaction carried out in 
anhydrous ether using 2 equiv. of DIBALH (solution in 
cyclohexane) at - 78 “c aflorded 2a in 15% yield. With 
3 .O equiv . of DIBALH in cyclohexane, the reaction in 
ether at - 90- - 140 “c afforded a complicated mixture 
(Entry 2, Table 1 ) . However, it is interesting to note 
that the corresponding reaction using the DIBAL-H solu- 
tion in toluene atforded 2a cleanly in 83% yield (Entry 
4, Table 1) , indicating that an interesting dramatic sol- 
vent effect occurred in this reduction. he typical results 
of the reduction of 2, 3-allenoates with DIBALH in 
toluene are summarized in Table 2. From Table 2 it can 
be seen that R’ can be aromatic, alkyl and H groups and 
Rz can be aromatic, beql, ally1 and alkyl pups and 
the yields range from 53% to 85%. However, with a 
carbon-carbon bond in the Rz subetituent , the reaction af- 
forded 2,3-denol 2c in 42% yield together with an un- 
identified product (Entry 3, Table 2) 
In conclusion, we have obse~ed a dramatic solvent 
effect in the reduction reaction of 2,3-allenoates using 
DIBALH as the reductant. So far the reason for this is 
not clear yet. With the convenient synthesis of 2,3-al- 
lenoates, lC” this method provides a facile route to 2,3- 
denoh. With our recent advances in the resolution of
